lines.text: Is a value an outlier? → compare it with $Q_{1} - 1.5 \times \mathrm{IQR}$ and $Q_{3} + 1.5 \times \mathrm{IQR}$ (4.1)
Predict $y$ from $x$ → regression line of $y$ on $x$. Predict $x$ from $y$ → line of $x$ on $y$. Only inside the range of the data (4.4, 4.10)
Two stages, with or without replacement → tree diagram: multiply along a path, add across paths (4.6)
“Given that” → $\mathrm{P}(A \mid B) = \frac{\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}$, with the given event on the bottom (4.6, 4.11)
Are $A$ and $B$ independent? → compare $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)$ with $\mathrm{P}(A)\,\mathrm{P}(B)$, then conclude (4.6, 4.11)
Unknown $k$ in a probability distribution → the probabilities add up to $1$. Fair game → $\mathrm{E}(X) = 0$ (4.7)
Fixed number of independent trials, two outcomes, same $p$ → binomial, $X \sim \mathrm{B}(n, p)$ (4.8)
Normal, value to probability → normal cdf. Probability to value → inverse normal, using the area to the left (4.9)
Normal with $\mu$ or $\sigma$ unknown → get $z$ from the inverse normal of $\mathrm{N}(0, 1)$, then solve $\frac{x - \mu}{\sigma} = z$ (4.12)
Probability of a first-stage event, given what happened next → Bayes' theorem: that path over every path to the given event (4.13)

Continuous random variable with pdf $f$ → probabilities by $\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$; median $m$ from $\int_{-\infty}^{m} f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{1}{2}$; $\mathrm{E}(X) = \int x f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ (4.14)
